subject: crab
reasoning:
I'm planning out a crab module using the SDK's builder functions—joints, parts, sweeps, and paint helpers—sketching dimensions for a body roughly a quarter meter wide before building out the legs and claws.

For the carapace shape, I'm deciding to use a loft along the z-axis with varying width and height stations to create a dome-like shell, narrower at front and rear and widest in the middle, rather than a lathe which would produce a disc instead of the ellipsoid dome I want. I'm placing the root body joint near the top of the shell and starting to define child joints for the eye stalks next.

Now I'm working out the leg chains—four legs per side, each built from a polyline of hip, knee, ankle, and foot points moving outward and down to the ground, with joint names like "hipL1", "kneeL1", "ankleL1", "footL1" so the four points create three spans with a proper tip joint at the foot.

For the geometry, I'm sweeping tapered tubes along each leg chain using a radius function that thins toward the tip, and planning the larger front claw arms (shoulder-elbow-wrist-hand) with pincer shapes extruded or swept at the wrist joint to form the chelipeds.

For the eyes, I'll build short stalks connecting to small spheres colored black and white. For the shell, I'm planning a mottled paint pattern in reds and oranges for coloring.

Still defining joints and rigging...

Still placing leg joints...

Still working out the claw geometry...

Checking orientation so left side matches +X since the shell faces +Z. Now setting up the eye stalks as small rods extending from the body front, with joints like "eyeStalkL" anchored near the base for proper hierarchy.

For the eyes themselves, I'm building tiny spheres at the stalk tips—a dark eyeball, possibly skipping a pupil or highlight for simplicity, and deciding to skip a mouth feature since crabs' mouthparts aren't essential here. For shell texture, I'm planning to use surface sampling to find points on the carapace and attach small bump spheres there for a textured, speckled look, and considering adding spikes along the front of the carapace too.

Working through coloring: a mottled red-orange for the shell and claws, warm orange stripes for the legs, dark eyes, and deciding to keep things simple by using mottle patterns everywhere rather than more complex custom paint functions for things like underside countershading.

Now I'm laying out the loft stations for the carapace (width/height at each z position so the body tapers front to back), adding a smaller tucked-under abdomen plate beneath it, and working out hip positions for the leg chains along the body's sides.

Each leg chain (hip-knee-ankle-foot) gets per-index z splay and x/y offsets so legs spread naturally and feet touch the ground plane at y=0, with a tapering sweep radius from thigh to foot tip. I'm naming joints consistently like hip0L, knee0L, ankle0L, foot0L, using string parent references to the body, and setting the leg chain role to auto-contact at the tip so the feet register as ground contacts.

Now I'm defining arm chains (shoulder-elbow-wrist-hand) with similar positioning logic, then building the pincer claws as two tapered sweeps attached to the hand joint, upper and lower, each with a shrinking radius function and rounded-to-pointed caps to form the claw shape.

For the eye, I'm setting up a stalk joint parented to the body with an aim direction toward the eye tip, attaching a white sphere eyeball and a smaller dark pupil sphere offset slightly forward, both rigidly bound to that stalk bone. Then I'm planning shell surface detail by creating a surface query on the shell sweep so I can place bumps or spots using nearest-point lookups.

I'm placing small light-colored bump spheres across a set of points on the shell's top surface, plus adding a few dark spike protrusions near the front edge using the same surface hits as oriented bases. Finally I'm sketching the overall module structure: a build function that creates the builder, assembles the crab, and returns the root, plus an exported meta object with name and description, and I'm considering which paint helper utilities (mottle, stripes, countershade) to import for coloring.

Now I'm setting up the body joint and leg chains: placing the body joint near the shell's base, then looping over left and right sides to build four leg chains each with hip, knee, ankle, and foot points positioned with slight z-offsets per leg so they splay naturally, tucking the hips just inside the shell's width.

Finishing the leg setup, I'm defining the sweep radii for legs (tapering from hip to foot) and setting up arm chains with shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand joints, tapering their sweep radii too so the pincers attach correctly at the hand joint tip.

I'm lofting the carapace and abdomen shapes from their station paths, then setting up procedural paint textures -- mottled coloring for the shell and claws, striped coloring for the legs, and countershading for the belly.

For the fine details, I'm adding spikes along the shell edges using nearest-surface lookups, small bumpy stick-on geometry for texture, and eye stalks built from rods with sphere-shaped eyes and pupils attached at specific joint positions. I'm making sure all the color and geometry parameters match the expected builder signatures before finalizing the code.
